Note that the denominator $\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3$ is always positive. We know this because

$$
-1\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x\le 1\,⇒\,2\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\le 4.
$$

So, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by $\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9-2x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3} & >\frac{x-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3} \\ (\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3)\cdot \frac{9-2x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3} & >(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3)\cdot \frac{x-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3} \\ 9-2x & >x-1 \\ -3x & >-10 \\ x & <\,\frac{10}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
